issue: Capability failure leaves `batch.status` as running, and a later successful retry does not clear its stale `control.attention`, violating the lifecycle contract and leaving completed state with failure attention
`ovcaq run --no-tui` and `ovcaq capability retry agoge` always select an unavailable capability runner, so required capabilities can never succeed through the installed public commands
Extract timeout-observation construction from `_collect`; the new function is 54 lines and exceeds the 50-line limit

Retry budgets can be dodged forever. `Supervisor._decide` resets `RetryState` whenever the failure class changes, and failure-path RETRY/WAIT decisions never advance `phase_repeats`. Alternating failures (agent death, then connectivity, then agent death...) therefore relaunch sessions without limit. This breaks the PRD's "Retry storms: Bound every wait/retry" mitigation. Confirmed by tracing `decide` and `_decide`

No production code ever starts a batch. Nothing in `src/` writes `batch.id` or `batch.status="running"`, and `new_state` leaves `batch.id=""`. So `ovcaq init` followed by `ovcaq run --no-tui` raises at `_open_session` → `publish_session_metric` → `_validate_identifier("")`, and `archive_final_state` also requires the id. The installed drain acceptance test passes only because its SEED script writes the batch fields straight through StateStore

A bootstrap repeat-stall (no PRD) returns PAUSE with exit 0 and writes no pause intent; the plan (§12.3 step 11) says halt. CI reads it as success, and every rerun burns another session before pausing again (test asserts `(0, PAUSE, 3)`)

`StateService.resume` always clears `pause_reason` but leaves `work.phase/next_phase == "paused"`. After a systemic park (records.py:445) or a `review_cap` pause, it erases the reason and the review_cap routing key that `workflow/resume.py:17` reads. Meanwhile `_boundary` still returns PAUSE, so `ovcaq run` exits 0 with 0 sessions and no explanation

The batch status lifecycle is incomplete. `apply(COMPLETE)` only archives, so a drain with no *required* capability (non-empty drain, or empty drain with only optional pending capabilities) archives `batch.status` still `running`. A failed capability never sets `batch.status="attention"`, which plan §8.6 step 5 requires

Capability timeout comes from the workflow phase route (`resolve_phase_route(work.phase or next_phase)`), not from capability config (plan §7 `[capabilities.agoge] timeout_seconds`). Startup `_reconcile_capabilities` resolves a full agent route (it needs agent config and a valid tier, and raises on phase `paused`) only to throw the timeout away

Reports count capability metric rows as workflow sessions. Canonical rows always carry `phase_launched` (None for capabilities) and `_metric_partitions` selects sessions by key presence. One capability attempt therefore inflates the session count and turns batch cost/token totals to unknown. No test covers it (test_canonical_metrics only has phase rows)
`_metric_partitions` silently drops any row whose `usage` is not a Mapping, using a `for usage in [...] if isinstance(...)` comprehension trick. That swallows an error and is hard to read

Extra `reconcile_metrics` calls. `CapabilityService._begin` rebuilds the aggregate right after publishing the pending row, so the aggregate shows the live capability attempt as `interrupted` for its whole run. `Supervisor._run_capability` calls it again after `finish`→`_finalize` already did

`Supervisor._run_capability` duplicates CapabilityService. It hand-builds `SessionPaths` that `_begin` already returned and `start` threw away, and re-implements `retry`'s run/finish-on-exception flow with a different failure detail (bare `str(error)` vs "runner raised …; retry X explicitly")

`_ResolvedModelClaudeDriver` inverts the tier map to turn the supervisor's resolved model back into a tier key so `ClaudeDriver` can resolve it again. The round trip is a subclass whose only job is undoing work

`DEFAULT_PHASE_TIERS = {"build": "sonnet", "review": "opus", ...}` lives in the provider-neutral `ovcaq.drivers` package init and feeds `config._supervisor_phases`. Neutral routing defaults are therefore Claude tier names: any agent without `sonnet`/`opus` tier keys fails with "Unknown agent tier" (AGENTS.md: model names live under their adapter)

Nothing in `src/` reads `SupervisorSettings.phases`. The supervisor routes through `resolve_phase_route(root, …)`, which rebuilds settings from disk (parsing both TOML files twice per call). So the validated `phases=` override and the `**explicit: object` runtime type checks in `supervisor_settings` only matter to tests

`_boundary` is a second, pre-launch decision table outside decision.py. It imports the private `_capability_decision` and ignores the `control.attention` that `decide` halts on, so a non-drained state with attention launches a session before halting (PRD: every halt is a pure, table-tested decision)

`test_incomplete_lifecycle_commands_fail_with_json_usage_errors` passes against the pre-change code, because unknown commands also return `usage`. It pins neither `run` requiring `--no-tui` nor `capability retry` requiring NAME (fail-first replay)

`record_state_failure` has no production caller. Supervisor state read/write failures return HALT without emergency evidence, so the `require_no_emergency_failure` gate never fires for a real failure and the next `ovcaq run` relaunches (plan §8.4)
`Supervisor.run` reconciles capabilities (a state write) before `require_no_emergency_failure`, so it writes state before checking whether the store was declared broken

`ovcaq stop` leaves no durable stopped outcome in state. The SIGTERM path only finalizes summary.json and the metric (`decision="halt"`), but plan §6 and §8.4 require "record the stopped outcome" as a supervisor-authored state outcome
